changes.original: Large language models (LLMs) add a different option: a general-purpose service that receives measurements as text and returns a diagnostic label, sometimes with an explanation, without task-specific training \citep{qaid2026explainable,zheng2024empirical,li2024chatgptphm}.
changes.replacement: Large language models (LLMs) add text-based approaches to diagnosis, including task-specific fine-tuning \citep{qaid2026explainable,zheng2024empirical} and broader foundation-model workflows for prognostics and health management \citep{li2024chatgptphm}. Here, we examine a general-purpose service that receives measurements as text and returns diagnostic labels without task-specific training.
changes.reason: Separate the published fine-tuning evidence from the present study’s API-only operating choice.

changes.original: FaultExplainer \citep{khan2025faultexplainer} & none & -- & -- & -- & \checkmark\ (TEP)
changes.replacement: FaultExplainer \citep{khan2025faultexplainer} & root-cause list supplied or withheld & -- & -- & -- & \checkmark\ (TEP)
changes.reason: Acknowledge the input-information comparison actually performed in FaultExplainer.

changes.original: Seventy runs, ten per class, form the main panel, following the run-level separation recommended for open process-monitoring benchmarks \citep{melo2022open}; each contributes one seeded late snapshot (sample index 200--500).
changes.replacement: Seventy runs, ten per class, form the main panel; we keep simulation runs disjoint across training and evaluation, and each main-panel run contributes one seeded late snapshot (sample index 200--500).
changes.reason: State the actual run-disjoint design without assigning an unverified specific recommendation to a general benchmark review.

changes.original: This is the test an evaluation with one call per condition would use; it treats all labels in a call as independent.
changes.replacement: This is the test an evaluation with one call per condition would use; it treats different test-case pairs as independent while retaining the paired comparison within each case.
changes.reason: McNemar preserves within-case pairing; its relevant assumption here is independence across case pairs, which shared-call dependence may violate.

changes.original: Each of the 52 numerical entries receives its documented descriptor and unit in the clean text representation; variable identities follow the TEP specification, with units checked against the original operating tables \citep{chen2014cognitive,ricker1995optimal}.
changes.replacement: Each of the 52 numerical entries receives a descriptor and unit in the clean text representation. Variable identities follow the TEP specification \citep{chen2014cognitive}; source descriptors and units are documented in Ricker's accompanying operating tables (Table~3 for the 41 measured variables and Table~4 for the first 11 manipulated variables) \citep{ricker1995optimal}.
changes.reason: Distinguishes variable-identity source from unit source and avoids claiming a complete implementation audit merely from citation checks.

changes.original: Industrial records add a physical constraint absent from most tabular benchmarks: each value is meaningful only together with its channel, name and unit, so a wrong association is a data-integrity fault rather than a formatting variant.
changes.replacement: For industrial records, the channel, name and unit specify the physical interpretation of each value; a wrong association is therefore a data-integrity fault rather than a formatting variant.
changes.reason: Removes an unsupported prevalence/novelty comparison while retaining the substantive physical interpretation.

changes.original: Behavioural testing frames such checks as invariance and directional tests \citep{ribeiro2020beyond}; our mapping faults and reorderings follow that logic.
changes.replacement: Behavioural testing distinguishes invariance tests from perturbations with specified directional expectations \citep{ribeiro2020beyond}. Our correct pair reorderings are invariance probes; mapping faults are error injections without a prescribed direction of diagnostic change.
changes.reason: The reference requires a specified expected direction for DIR; mapping corruption alone does not supply one.

changes.original: In long inputs, information in the middle is used less than information at the start or end \citep{liu2024lost}
changes.replacement: In long-context question answering and key--value retrieval, performance often declines when relevant information is placed in the middle rather than at the start or end \citep{liu2024lost}
changes.reason: Adds the studied task scope and avoids an unconditional universal claim.

changes.original: majority voting over sampled reasoning paths improves accuracy \citep{wang2023selfconsistency}
changes.replacement: voting over answers from sampled reasoning paths improved accuracy on arithmetic and commonsense benchmarks \citep{wang2023selfconsistency}
changes.reason: Scopes empirical gains to the cited tasks and uses answer-level aggregation precisely.

changes.original: LIFT showed that classification and regression tasks can be solved by writing features as sentences \citep{dinh2022lift}
changes.replacement: LIFT fine-tuned language models for classification and regression using features and targets expressed as text \citep{dinh2022lift}
changes.reason: Restores the essential supervised fine-tuning step; text serialization alone is not the tested method.

changes.original: Because the best method differs between panels, we report the range over all six methods rather than a single reference chosen on test scores \citep{tan2024useful}; per-method results and hyperparameters are in Supplementary Appendix~H.
changes.replacement: Because the best method differs between panels, we report the range over all six methods rather than a single reference chosen on test scores; per-method results and hyperparameters are in Supplementary Appendix~H.
changes.reason: Removes a citation attached to a specific local reporting choice that the source did not establish; retain the valid related-work citation.

changes.original: six regimes found by $k$-means on the operating settings, the usual practice for this subset \citep{ramasso2014benchmarking}
changes.replacement: six regimes found by $k$-means on the operating settings, following earlier C-MAPSS preprocessing strategies reviewed by \citet{ramasso2014benchmarking}
changes.reason: The source provides preprocessing precedents but not a prevalence claim for FD002.

changes.original: and designs in which items are crossed with other sampled factors require crossed random effects or equivalent resampling \citep{baayen2008mixed,bates2015lme4,owen2007pigeonhole}. In LLM evaluation the repeated call is such a factor, but it is rarely treated as one.
changes.replacement: and inference for designs with crossed sampled factors should account for both factors, for example through crossed random effects or an appropriately designed resampling scheme \citep{baayen2008mixed,bates2015lme4,owen2007pigeonhole}. In the present LLM evaluation, repeated calls form one such factor.
changes.reason: Removes an unsupported field-wide prevalence claim and avoids implying automatic equivalence of all crossed models and resampling schemes.

changes.original: We report coverage, accepted-label error, usable correct yield and calls per \emph{window}, not per individual diagnosis \citep{geifman2017selective}.
changes.replacement: We report coverage and accepted-label error \citep{geifman2017selective}, together with usable correct yield and calls per \emph{window}, not per individual diagnosis.
changes.reason: Attaches the citation to risk–coverage concepts rather than the locally defined yield and call-budget units.

changes.original: a pattern traced to positional attention bias \citep{hsieh2024found}
changes.replacement: a pattern associated with positional attention bias and mitigated by attention calibration in the studied models \citep{hsieh2024found}
changes.reason: Preserve the demonstrated association/intervention without implying a uniquely established causal explanation.

changes.original: dispersion over repeated answers underlies black-box uncertainty and hallucination measures \citep{kuhn2023semantic,xiong2024uncertainty,manakul2023selfcheckgpt}
changes.replacement: dispersion over repeated answers underlies uncertainty and hallucination measures \citep{kuhn2023semantic,xiong2024uncertainty,manakul2023selfcheckgpt}
changes.reason: Kuhn2023 uses generation probabilities; do not classify all cited methods as requiring only black-box sampled text.

changes.original: For time series more broadly, LLMs have been reprogrammed or prompted for forecasting \citep{jin2024time,gruver2023large,liu2024large}, but ablations show that removing the language model often does not hurt accuracy \citep{tan2024useful}, and strong models reason poorly over raw series \citep{merrill2024struggle,jin2024position}.
changes.replacement: For time series more broadly, LLMs have been reprogrammed or prompted for forecasting \citep{jin2024time,gruver2023large,liu2024large}, but ablations show that removing the language model often does not hurt accuracy \citep{tan2024useful}. Direct evaluation has found weaknesses in zero-shot reasoning over time-series tasks \citep{merrill2024struggle}, while a position study illustrates limitations in interpreting time-series patterns and explaining classifications \citep{jin2024position}.
changes.reason: Separate the direct zero-shot benchmark from the illustrative position study; incorporate both audits.

changes.original: and testing laboratories analyse reference materials alongside unknown samples to ensure the validity of their results \citep{iso17025}.
